data.name: Battle Knights
data.detailed_description:
Play as the blue knight, Wonder, who is on a quest to unite the colored realms.

Battle Knights is the kind of game you remember playing back in the days of the NES and SNES. It's an easy to play yet challenging platformer. The game may seem trivial with Wonder only being able to attack, block, and jump but, rest assured, that Battle Knights is not for the faint of heart.

Featuring 4 game modes (Story, Versus, Dungeon Run, and Survival) and unlockable content, you're sure to find something that suits you.

Story Mode:

Battle Knights contains a story mode that consists of six realms that the player must clear in order to beat the game. The realms area playable in any order the player wishes, with a boss being unlocked after the completion of each realm.

Story mode can also be played cooperatively. All realms feature a challenge level that will unlock a bonus mode once all are beaten.

Six Realms to clear
Coop (Up to 2 players)
Challenge levels
Bosses
Unlockable content
Versus Mode:

Battle Knights also contains a versus component containing 14 stages that can be played with up to six players locally. Versus Mode can be played in any team combination (2v2, 3v3, 2v2v2, 1v3, etc) or free for all. Knights of the same color are automatically placed on the same team. This means that to play a free for all match, all players must select differing knight colors.

Unlike Story Mode, Versus Mode has items that drop and, upon pickup, give the player a temporary ability. The frequency at which the items drop can be changed or removed completely if the players are wanting a more skill-based match.

2-6 player competitive mode
Teams in any combination (3v3, 2v2, 1v2, 1v3, etc) or free for all
Same colored knights are automatically grouped into the same team
Last man/team standing wins
Item spawns (frequency can be changed or disabled entirely)

Bonus Modes:
Some available at the start
Others must be unlocked through story mode
Includes 1-6 player coop modes

reviews.review:
Battle Knights is a compact 2D action platformer that embraces the straightforward design principles of classic console games. Developed and published by Mire Studios, it places players in control of Wonder, a blue knight tasked with traveling across colorful realms and bringing them together. Instead of relying on complicated character progression, large inventories, or sprawling environments, the game concentrates on movement, timing, combat, blocking, and surviving increasingly demanding situations. Its intentionally simple foundation makes it easy to understand, while the challenge provides the incentive to improve.

The core controls revolve around a small selection of actions, including jumping, attacking, and blocking. This makes Battle Knights approachable within minutes, but understanding the controls is considerably easier than mastering them. Enemies and environmental obstacles gradually demand better timing and more disciplined movement, encouraging players to learn from unsuccessful attempts. There is an unmistakable old-school mentality behind the difficulty, with success depending primarily on execution rather than upgrades that allow players to overpower troublesome encounters.

Story Mode serves as the main progression-focused portion of the game and takes Wonder through six distinct realms. A welcome feature is the freedom to approach these realms in different orders instead of following one rigid sequence. Each area eventually leads toward a boss battle, providing a clear objective and giving individual realms a satisfying conclusion. Additional challenge levels encourage players to revisit the game's mechanics from a more demanding perspective, while completing objectives can contribute toward unlocking extra content.

The campaign can also be experienced cooperatively with two players. Cooperative play changes the atmosphere considerably, turning difficult platforming and combat sections into opportunities for coordination. This is especially appealing for players who prefer sharing retro-style adventures rather than tackling every challenge alone. Remote Play Together support also helps extend the usefulness of its local multiplayer design when two players cannot physically use the same computer.

Competitive multiplayer represents another important part of the package. Versus Mode accommodates up to six local players across 14 stages, providing considerably larger matches than might be expected from such a modest platformer. Team arrangements are flexible, allowing conventional balanced matches alongside uneven battles, multiple teams, and free-for-all competition. Character colors provide an immediate indication of team membership, keeping the rules understandable even when several knights occupy the screen simultaneously.

Versus battles are further altered by collectible items that temporarily provide different abilities. Players can adjust how frequently these items appear or disable them altogether. This is a useful customization option because groups looking for unpredictable party-game chaos can make power-ups more prominent, while players interested in skill-oriented competition can minimize their influence. Combined with the uncomplicated controls, this makes multiplayer accessible to newcomers without removing the possibility of experienced players developing better timing and defensive techniques.

Dungeon Run and Survival provide alternatives to the standard campaign and competitive matches, while additional bonus modes expand the available activities. Some bonus content is immediately accessible, whereas other portions require progress through Story Mode. Several activities support cooperative groups of up to six players, giving Battle Knights a stronger multiplayer identity than its simple appearance initially suggests. Steam Achievements, Steam Cloud, local shared or split-screen functionality, Remote Play Together, and Family Sharing complement these modes.

The pixel-based presentation reinforces the game's retro intentions. Rather than attempting highly elaborate visual effects, Battle Knights favors clear characters, colorful environments, and straightforward animation. The different knight colors are particularly practical during multiplayer matches because players and teams can be identified quickly. The visual approach is functional and charming enough for its purpose, although anyone expecting exceptionally detailed modern pixel art or cinematic presentation may consider it fairly modest.

Its simplicity is simultaneously one of its greatest strengths and most noticeable limitations. The small collection of actions makes Battle Knights immediately accessible, but combat can become repetitive for players accustomed to extensive weapon systems, elaborate combos, skill trees, or constantly evolving abilities. Likewise, its demanding encounters may frustrate players who prefer forgiving platformers. The experience works best when approached as an intentionally traditional action game in which repetition, pattern recognition, and mechanical improvement are fundamental parts of progression.

On Steam Deck, Battle Knights does not have an official Valve Steam Deck compatibility rating displayed as Verified or Playable. Its relatively lightweight 2D nature and controller-oriented gameplay make it the sort of game that may be suitable for handheld play, but the absence of an official compatibility classification means the experience should not be treated as formally guaranteed. Players interested specifically in Steam Deck use should therefore expect that configuration adjustments or compatibility-layer considerations may occasionally be necessary. Local multiplayer is also naturally less convenient on the handheld unless additional controllers are connected.

Battle Knights ultimately offers more variety than its basic retro presentation initially implies. Six campaign realms, boss battles, optional challenges, cooperative Story Mode, six-player competitive matches, Survival, Dungeon Run, unlockable activities, customizable items, and multiple team configurations create a respectable amount of content around a deliberately uncomplicated mechanical foundation. It is particularly attractive as a local multiplayer game, although determined solo players can still enjoy working through its campaign challenges.

As a whole, Battle Knights succeeds by understanding the kind of experience it wants to provide. It is not an expansive action RPG or an elaborate modern platforming spectacle, but rather a focused throwback built around responsive fundamentals, challenge, replayable modes, and couch multiplayer. Its limited mechanical depth and modest production values prevent it from standing among the most ambitious games in the genre, yet its accessible controls and generous multiplayer flexibility give it personality. For players who appreciate demanding retro platformers or need a straightforward local multiplayer game for a group, it provides an enjoyable if somewhat specialized experience.

Rating: 6/10
